section_summary: This section documents the political crises, cabinet reorganizations, and administrative restructuring in Japan from late August 1939 to mid-January 1940. Following the announcement of the German-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact, Prime Minister Kiichiro Hiranuma's cabinet resigned to assume responsibility, leading to the formation of a government under General Nobuyuki Abe with military leadership dominating key posts and attempts to reorient foreign policy. Facing mounting popular and parliamentary discontent over price inflation, commodity shortages, and ineffective economic controls—culminating in a Diet resolution signed by 250 members demanding his resignation—Premier Abe resigned in January 1940, leading to deliberations that culminated in the formation of the Yonai Cabinet.

subfiles.about: Comprehensive political report reviewing cabinet expansion, party overtures, administrative paralysis, price control revisions, and military armaments policy.
subfiles.summary: A five-page extract from American Embassy Tokyo Despatch No. 4377 (Periodic Report No. 144 for November 1939) reviewing internal Japanese political conditions. It details the appointments of Kiyoshi Akita (Welfare) and Hidejiro Nagata (Railways), marking the formal abandonment of Abe's small-cabinet concept, alongside Minseito leader Chuji Machida's refusal to accept a portfolio. The report examines entrenched bureaucratic opposition that stalled the proposed Trade Ministry and civil service tenure reform, reviews Commerce Minister Godo's adoption of 'appropriate prices' amidst severe commodity inflation and market hoarding, and analyzes public statements by Premier Abe and War Minister Shunroku Hata stressing army replenishment and continental defense against potential rivals.
subfiles.title: Report Extract on Internal Political Conditions in Japan (Despatch No. 4377 / Periodic Report No. 144)
